climate.overview_html: COP31 talks in Antalya enter their final days with an 18-page first draft cover decision that calls for accelerated action to phase out fossil fuels. A separate draft on the UN carbon market drew EU, Swiss and Senegalese opposition to reopening project-developer rules. The summit is scheduled to close on Nov 20.

items.headline: COP31 first draft calls for accelerated action to phase out fossil fuels
items.summary: Negotiations lead Chris Bowen published an 18-page draft cover decision that also sets electricity at 35% of final energy by 2035. Bowen said provisions without consensus will be cut from later drafts before the Nov 20 close.

items.headline: Developing-country blocs push to loosen UN carbon market rules at COP31
items.summary: Like-Minded Developing Countries and least developed and landlocked states questioned requirements on carbon-credit project developers. The EU, Switzerland and Senegal oppose reassessing the rules; a first draft decision was published late Saturday.

major_events.name: Cyclone Akvan, Bay of Bengal
major_events.impact: IMD forecasts landfall between Nellore and Tuni around noon Nov 20 with winds of 120-130 km/h gusting to 145 km/h. Odisha has deployed 74 rescue teams and begun evacuations in southern districts (Business Standard).

major_events.name: Pacific Northwest atmospheric rivers, US
major_events.impact: A third atmospheric river in four days was forecast to peak Nov 16 over Washington and Oregon, with river flooding and high winds into Tuesday (FOX Weather).

weather.overview_html: Cyclone Akvan is forecast to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast around noon on Nov 20 with gusts to 145 km/h, the state's third cyclone since Oct 28. Odisha has started evacuations and fishing operations at Visakhapatnam are halted. In the US, another atmospheric river peaked over the Pacific Northwest on Nov 16 after two storms on Nov 13-14.

items.headline: IMD expects Cyclone Akvan to hit Andhra Pradesh, its third cyclone since Oct 28
items.summary: Akvan is forecast to cross between Nellore and Tuni around noon on Nov 20 with winds of 120-130 km/h gusting to 145 km/h. It follows Cyclone Arnab on Oct 28 and Cyclone Murasu on Nov 3.

items.headline: Andhra Pradesh and Odisha on alert as Cyclone Akvan nears the coast
items.summary: IMD issued heavy rain, thunderstorm and gusty wind alerts for coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Rayalaseema. The Coast Guard and fisheries officials recalled trawlers and halted operations at Visakhapatnam Fishing Harbour.

items.headline: Atmospheric river to peak over the Pacific Northwest on Nov 16
items.summary: Heavy rain, river flooding and high winds were forecast to continue into Tuesday. The storm follows atmospheric rivers that hit the region on Nov 13-14.

items.headline: Two atmospheric rivers hit Oregon and Washington back to back
items.summary: NWS Seattle warned of swells up to 20 feet on the Washington coast. Forecasters flagged flash flooding, urban flooding and landslides.

items.headline: PAGASA says one more typhoon may enter Philippine area before year-end
items.summary: PAGASA expects at least one more tropical cyclone in its area of responsibility before the end of 2026. Typhoon Cempaka, the 32nd named storm of the western North Pacific season, recurved without entering it.

renewables.overview_html: Adding wind to solar and batteries cuts the median cost of meeting 90% of demand to $86/MWh from $105/MWh, Ember found. Solcast data put October irradiance 14% above normal around the Great Lakes and 9% below in the Southwest. Australia's regulator fined EnergyAustralia AU$750,000 over batteries that allegedly failed to deliver frequency services.

items.headline: Ember finds adding wind cuts firm solar-plus-storage power to $86/MWh
items.summary: Adding wind lowers the median cost of meeting 90% of demand from $105/MWh to $86/MWh, and by about two-fifths in northern regions. In Germany, the worst combined wind-solar week of the decade leaves a deficit of about five days of average demand, against six for either source alone.

items.headline: Solcast puts October irradiance 14% above normal around the Great Lakes
items.summary: Buffalo and Cleveland set October irradiance records. Rain and persistent cloud pushed irradiance 9% below normal across the US Southwest and northern Mexico.

items.headline: Sri Lanka report blames a coal unit, not solar, for the Oct 17 blackout
items.summary: Norochcholai Unit 1 fell from 187 MW to 5 MW within 450 ms and grid frequency dropped from 49.906 Hz to 47.5 Hz in two seconds. Early official comments had blamed excess solar output.

items.headline: EnergyAustralia pays AU$750,000 over alleged battery FCAS failures
items.summary: The Australian Energy Regulator issued 10 infringement notices over four batteries in NSW and Victoria that allegedly could not deliver frequency control offers in 2023-24. EnergyAustralia self-reported and made no admission of a breach.

items.headline: Sif closes one monopile line and seeks bridge financing
items.summary: The Dutch monopile maker will shut one of three lines at Maasvlakte 2. It reported material uncertainty about continuing as a going concern while its largest project awaits a final investment decision.

science.overview_html: A Nature Reviews Earth & Environment review says Arctic sea ice is likely to enter a rapid loss event before 2040, which could bring the first ice-free summer within five years. A GRL paper uses the sea-level budget gap to infer stronger heat uptake below 2,000 m since the mid-2010s. The State of Wildfires report finds climate change tripled the odds of Iberia's August 2025 fire weather.

items.headline: Review warns rapid Arctic ice loss events could start before 2040
items.summary: Such an event could bring the first ice-free summer within five years of onset; the satellite record shows two, in 2001-2008 and 2014-2020. The authors say climate models generally miss extreme breakup events and call for early-warning systems.

items.headline: Sea-level budget gap points to stronger deep-ocean heat uptake since mid-2010s
items.summary: The authors convert the sea-level budget residual into heat uptake below 2,000 m, which Argo does not sample. Added to measured ocean heat uptake, the total matches the CERES energy imbalance for 2015-2024 within uncertainty; they call the deep signal possible, not confirmed.

items.headline: State of Wildfires report says climate change tripled odds of Iberia's 2025 fire weather
items.summary: The August 2025 fire weather in northwest Iberia was about three times more likely and burned area about three times larger due to warming, per the Met Office. The season had 14 megafires and over 40,000 evacuations; figures may change in review.

items.title: ICEYE unveils Gen5 radar satellite with 11 cm government imaging mode
items.body_html: ICEYE's fifth-generation SAR satellite reaches 11 cm resolution at 1,800 MHz for governments and 16 cm for other customers, with downlink up to 1 Gbps. ICEYE gave no launch date or pricing; the onboard AI processor is a roadmap item for in-orbit screening.

items.title: Windy makes meteoblue AI the default model in its location forecast
items.body_html: Windy's latest release sets the meteoblue AI multimodel as the default point forecast, replacing ECMWF there while ECMWF stays the map default. The update also adds team dashboards and a lightning archive, and Windy says NOAA's RRFS will follow as its NAM replacement.

items.title: Royal Navy picks Ocean Infinity for £90M Atlantic Net sensor network
items.body_html: The UK framework, worth up to £90M, has Ocean Infinity integrate uncrewed vessels, underwater sensors and data services across the North Atlantic. It is the first phase of Atlantic Bastion, which later moves the role to Navy-owned Type 92 surface and Type 93 underwater drones.
